principle: Atmosphere may support orientation, but it must never fabricate historical evidence, private belief, causal mechanism, soundscape, social structure or religious meaning beyond the cited source boundary.

moments.title: Pigment, shell, coast
moments.place: Cueva de los Aviones · Iberian Mediterranean coast
moments.scene: A coastal cave context. Marine shells, ochre and pigment residues survive where intentions do not.
moments.interpretation: The assemblage supports deliberate material selection and modification. Symbolic display is plausible in the cited research context, but a specific religion, deity, ritual script or private belief is not directly recoverable.
moments.unknown: Who used the objects, what they called them, whether every object carried the same meaning, and whether the behavior belonged to ritual, identity display, aesthetics, technology or overlapping practices.

moments.title: A body placed, a meaning uncertain
moments.scene: A rock-shelter landscape. Human burials survive as spatial relationships between body, sediment and objects. Theology does not fossilize with them.
survives: Excavation observations relevant to funerary interpretation
moments.interpretation: Structured mortuary behavior is supported at the site. That can inform hypotheses about social treatment of the dead without establishing an afterlife doctrine or formal religion.
moments.unknown: The mourners' concepts of personhood, death, ancestors or afterlife; the emotional meaning of a burial; and whether mortuary actions were religious, social, practical, symbolic or inseparably mixed.

moments.title: Ochre was not one thing
moments.scene: Layered cave deposits preserve repeated human activity. Ochre can participate in technology and display at the same site, warning against a single universal meaning.
moments.interpretation: Some ochre pieces functioned as lithic retouchers. This is positive evidence against treating every pigment artifact as automatically symbolic or ritual.
moments.unknown: Whether the same pieces also carried social or symbolic significance, how uses changed through time, and how people categorized material, color or technique.

image.role: SITE STRATIGRAPHY CONTEXT · NOT HISTORICAL RECONSTRUCTION

moments.title: A deliberate line, not a decoded message
moments.scene: A small silcrete flake carries deliberate red-ochre lines. Intention survives at the level of mark-making; the code behind the mark does not.
survives: Microscopic and chemical evidence of deliberate drawing
moments.interpretation: The object supports deliberate graphic production and capacity for designed visual marking. It does not establish writing, ritual use or religious content.
moments.unknown: What the design referred to, whether it communicated to others, how common the convention was, and whether its significance was aesthetic, mnemonic, social, ritual or something outside modern categories.

moments.title: Careful deposition, cautious interpretation
moments.scene: A limestone rockshelter in Dordogne. A child's body and a dug pit provide unusually concrete mortuary evidence; cosmology remains beyond direct observation.
survives: A pit cut into sterile sediment
A young Neanderthal child placed within the feature
moments.interpretation: Purposeful deposition is supported for this context. Specific funerary theology, ancestor belief or afterlife concepts are not identified by the burial alone.
moments.unknown: The social relationship to the child, emotional experience, spoken practices, concepts of death and whether repeated mortuary customs had shared meanings.
